creative_intent: Generate a precision product photograph of a front-facing, matte white boron-carbide ceramic industrial component with exact symmetrical hard-surface geometry, clean beveled edges, and visible mounting holes, focusing on a clean technical ceramic material study.

must_have: exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

composition.background: minimal environment, controlled shadow, premium studio isolation

constraints: color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Ensure the manufactured object is clearly readable and present.
Prevent any abstract or atmospheric drift.
Maintain a clear and distinct industrial object silhouette.
Strictly avoid texture-only or surface-only interpretations that lose the object.
Lock the object read and prevent abstract drift.
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
success_criteria: Achieve a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read.
Ensure dry, dense, engineered manufactured-object readability.
Confirm the presence of a readable industrial object silhouette.
Verify the material-only scope is maintained without losing the manufactured object read.
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
direction_summary: Prioritize a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, focusing on dry, dense, engineered manufactured-object readability. Suppress plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral banding, sedimentary drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, and toy-like finish. Preserve material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read, ensuring a clear industrial component is visible.
